sources.authors: Gheorghe Tecuci; Mihai Boicu; Cristina Boicu; Dorin Marcu; Bogdan Stanescu; Marcel Barbulescu
sources.title: The Disciple–RKF Learning and Reasoning Agent

implemented: Authors report expert-guided acquisition of domain rules in an August 1999 exercise and subsequent use of the RKF family in instruction.
learned: Generalized rules from expert examples and explanations; refinement through feedback.
designed: Agent shell, initial ontology, teaching interface, rule-learning machinery, task domain and expert assistance.
limit: Expert supplies semantic knowledge and difficult reasoning; not autonomous discovery of underlying objectives. Programme affiliation is stated in 2000 paper (DARPA/AFOSR HPKB), exact award not established.
ora: Attribute learned rules to the information source, distinguish acquiring domain competence from autonomous acquisition without a teacher.
rights: Public metadata and original analysis only; no full source redistribution.

sources.authors: Khin Hua Ng; Zhiyuan Du; Gee Wah Ng
sources.title: DSO Cognitive Architecture: Unified Reasoning with Integrative Memory Using Global Workspace Theory
sources.access: Public abstract and affiliations; full chapter subscription restricted
sources.institution: Cognition and Fusion Lab 2, DSO National Laboratories, Singapore

implemented: 2010 prototype reportedly combines perceptual and contextual information for image recognition; 2017 authors describe an integrative-memory design and image-captioning example.
learned: No autonomous acquisition result verified in these primary abstracts; survey claims about training data remain leads for later primary review.
designed: Hierarchical structure, distributed memory, parallel information flow, global-workspace-inspired integration.
limit: Neither general intelligence nor subjective consciousness established; 2017 full methods not accessible in this batch.
ora: Integration and context use must be distinguished from acquired competence and verified against explicit inputs.
rights: Public metadata and original analysis only; no full source redistribution.

sources.authors: Boicho N. Kokinov; Alexander A. Petrov
sources.title: Integrating Memory and Reasoning in Analogy-Making: The AMBR Model
sources.access: Public author-hosted abstract and chapter metadata
sources.institution: New Bulgarian University; Bulgarian Academy of Science (Kokinov)

implemented: Context-dependent reasoning example in 1994; 2001 AMBR model simulates context and memory-distortion phenomena through interacting microprocesses.
learned: Specific durable learning effects not verified in inspected abstracts; dynamic activity and representations alone do not establish retention.
designed: Symbolic/connectionist micro-agent framework and supplied processing rules.
limit: Modeling memory distortion and analogy is not independent origin of learning mechanisms; no general transfer or E3 replication established.
ora: Emergent coordination is compatible with a designed substrate; separate state-dependent behavior from persistent acquired change.
rights: Public metadata and original analysis only; no full source redistribution.

sources.authors: David E. Meyer; David E. Kieras
sources.title: A computational theory of executive cognitive processes and multiple-task performance: Part 1. Basic mechanisms
sources.access: Public NLM bibliographic record and author abstract

implemented: Computational account of human concurrent cognitive and sensorimotor task performance; authors report application to human-computer interaction models.
learned: No independent acquisition of executive machinery established by inspected abstracts.
designed: Production-rule processor, sensory and motor components, executive control model.
limit: Human performance modeling and predictive fit are not evidence of autonomous development; full model fitting and competing explanations not assessed.
ora: Behavioral fit and cognitive mechanism provenance require separate evidence.
rights: Public metadata and original analysis only; no full source redistribution.

sources.authors: Smadar T. Kedar; Kathleen B. McKusick
sources.title: There is No Free Lunch: Tradeoffs in the Utility of Learned Knowledge
sources.access: Official public PDF; printed pp. 7 and 9 visually checked; NTRS marks US government work public use permitted

implemented: Simplified ERE/MTR implementation evaluated in a grid simulator with faulty initial operator models; authors report improved goal achievement but rising computational cost.
learned: Refined missing operator conditions and alternative action outcomes from prediction mismatches.
designed: Goal specification, domain representation, actions, repair methods, planner/reactor, metrics and simulator.
limit: 10 runs in one restricted test domain; simplified software; raw runs and code not independently recovered. Search and matching costs are proxy measures, not metabolic accounting. Dynamic performance monitor described as future work in 1992.
ora: Improved prediction or task success can cost more resources. Evaluate both costs and outcomes, without assuming more knowledge implies viability.
rights: Public metadata and original analysis only; no full source redistribution.
